logline: The agents of a Parisian talent agency manage their celebrity clients' disasters while their own professional and personal lives collapse in equal measure - a comedy of institutional dysfunction and real feeling.

renewal.note: The series concluded after four seasons in 2020. Creator Fanny Herrero confirmed Season 4 as the finale. An international English-language remake Ten Percent aired on BritBox in 2022. A feature film continuation was announced for 2026.

bollymeter.basis: 100% on Rotten Tomatoes from 7 reviews; IMDb 8.3 across the full series run. Creator Fanny Herrero's debut season established the show's distinctive formula of celebrity-episode architecture and genuine emotional intelligence.

seasons.review_body: Call My Agent! (original French title: Dix pour cent) launched on France 2 in October 2015, created by Fanny Herrero. The six-episode debut season follows four agents at the ASK talent agency - Andrea, Mathias, Gabriel, and Arlette - as they manage celebrity clients through fictional personal crises while their own lives run parallel disasters. Rotten Tomatoes gives Season 1 a perfect 100 percent from seven critics. The show's structural innovation is the celebrity-episode format: each hour built around a real French star playing a heightened version of themselves, lending authentic texture to the showbiz satire. The ensemble of Camille Cottin, Thibault de Montalembert, Gregory Montel, and Liliane Rovere generates genuine warmth beneath the comedy of professional chaos.

episode_reviews.title: Cecile de France
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: The premiere establishes the agency's four agents and the founding crisis that will define the season: a potential merger that threatens their independence. Cecile de France plays herself with a willingness to be unflattering; the show's comic-emotional tonal register is established in the first episode.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The first scene that makes clear this is a comedy that intends to mean something - the agent-client dynamic inverted.

bollymeter.basis: Series-level IMDb 8.3 sustained; critical consensus held near-unanimously positive across all four seasons. Season 2 refined the formula with stronger celebrity casting.

seasons.review_body: Season 2 aired April 2017, continuing the ASK agency's professional and personal entanglements. The celebrity-episode format was refined; the show brought in French stars with greater recognition across the series run. No separate Rotten Tomatoes aggregate exists for Season 2, but trade and critical coverage maintained the show's reputation as the benchmark French comedy of its era. The ensemble dynamics deepened; secondary characters acquired fuller backstories. The show's combination of sharp industry satire and unguarded emotional honesty kept audience ratings near the series average.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 2 refines the celebrity-episode format with stronger guest casting and deeper ensemble character work; the formula holds without diminishing returns.

bollymeter.basis: Widely regarded as the series peak, with the Isabelle Huppert episode cited by multiple reviewers as the single best hour in the show's run. IMDb series average 8.3.

seasons.review_body: Season 3 is widely cited by critics and the Arts Desk as the series at its best. The November 2018 season's Isabelle Huppert episode closed the run and is frequently identified as the single finest hour in the show - a masterclass in using celebrity persona as comedy engine while delivering real emotional weight. The season's writing was tightest across the three-season peak. By this point the show had accumulated international critical recognition and was becoming essential European television viewing.
seasons.season_over_season: Season 3 represents the show's creative peak; the Isabelle Huppert finale episode is cited by multiple outlets as the best single hour in the series run.

episode_reviews.title: Isabelle Huppert
episode_reviews.spoiler_free: Isabelle Huppert plays herself with a commitment to being genuinely difficult, and the season finale uses that persona to deliver both the show's funniest episode and its most emotionally resonant close. Critics across multiple outlets identified this as the best single episode Call My Agent! produced.
episode_reviews.the_moment: The final scene with Huppert and Andrea - the celebrity format at its most fully realised.

critic_note.text: The Isabelle Huppert finale does not have sheer brilliance - it has the best episode the series ever produced.

bollymeter.basis: 95% on Rotten Tomatoes from 22 critics; 100% audience score; won the International Emmy Award for Best Comedy Series in 2021. A fitting, emotionally honest farewell for the ensemble.

pull_quotes.text: The ending is strangely touching - a final bow that earns its sentiment.

seasons.review_body: Season 4 aired October 2020 as the confirmed series finale, and it honoured the obligation: guest stars Sigourney Weaver, Jean Reno, and Charlotte Gainsbourg provided the celebrity-episode architecture, while the ASK agents were given an ending that earned its emotional weight. Rotten Tomatoes critics approved at 95 percent from 22 reviews, and the audience returned a perfect 100 percent score. In November 2021, Call My Agent! won the International Emmy Award for Best Comedy Series, the capstone on a four-season run that had quietly become one of the strongest European comedy-dramas of the streaming era. The Arts Desk called the ending strangely touching.
seasons.season_over_season: The farewell season delivers the ensemble's resolution with the same structural grace as earlier seasons; the International Emmy win confirmed the series' standing as European streaming's best comedy.
